Validate the model, on a stated basis

Source: R/validation.R
mm_validate.Rd

Returns one row per basis, because the three numbers a clinical prediction paper reports are not interchangeable and presenting one as another is the commonest way a published model flatters itself.

Usage

mm_validate(model, cohort, B = 200L, full_process = FALSE)

Arguments

model

A mm_model().

cohort

The cohort, for held-out scoring and the split. Its development rows must be the ones the model was fitted on.

B

Bootstrap resamples.

full_process

Also run the full-process bootstrap. Off by default because it refits B times and costs accordingly.

Value

An object of class mm_validation: a data frame of metrics by basis, plus what produced them.

Details

The bases are:

  • apparent, the model scored on the rows it was fitted to. Always optimistic, reported so that the optimism is visible.

  • bootstrap, fixed model, from rms::validate(). Each resample refits the same formula, which corrects the optimism of estimating coefficients. It does not repeat imputation, selection, tuning or interaction screening, so it is not validation of a modelling strategy that includes those steps. The specification requires that distinction be made rather than assumed, and this column is where it is made.

  • held out, rows the project's split reserved. Scored once.

  • bootstrap, full process, with full_process = TRUE. Refits the whole strategy inside every resample, so the optimism corrected includes the data-dependent choices the fixed-model bootstrap inherits. See mm_full_process() for what it does and does not re-execute.

Incomplete rows

Every basis is judged on the rows that can be judged, and the exclusions are reported rather than absorbed. mm_evaluable() is the one rule, the same one mm_model() fitted under, so the sample a model is measured against is the sample it was estimated on; validating against a cohort whose development rows do not match the fit is an error rather than a quietly different number. The bootstraps resample the fitted cohort, never the supplied frame.

A missing predictor and a missing outcome are counted apart, with the overlap separately, because they are different exclusions and because taking a missing outcome for a non-event leaves the event count unchanged while inflating the denominator.

Rows are selected first and mm_predict() is then called at its own default of on_missing = "stop", so the complete-case path is explicit here and prediction keeps refusing to put a number on an incomplete record.

This is complete-case analysis. It is a computational strategy and not a guarantee: the estimates assume the exclusions are uninformative, which is an assumption rather than a finding, and the note column says so whenever any row was excluded. Multiple imputation is not in this package yet.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 1)
project <- mm_project("uds", "event", c("age", "bmi", "sex"),
                      cohort = cohort, split_var = "year",
                      split_at = 2023)
fit <- mm_model(project, cohort, nonlinear = "age")
#> Warning: the development sample may be too small for this model: 190 rows is 1928 short of the 2118 a model of 5 parameter(s) needs at 8.4% prevalence for 90% shrinkage. Coefficients from a sample this size are expected to be overfitted; see the adequacy element of the returned object.
mm_validate(fit, cohort, B = 25)
#> <mm_validation>  full-process: FALSE
#>   apparent                 n=190   events=16   C=0.6257 (0.4652-0.7862)  slope=1.0000
#>   bootstrap, fixed model   n=190   events=16   C=0.5010  slope=0.3818
#>   held out                 n=110   events=12   C=0.3844 (0.2074-0.5613)  slope=-1.1131
#>   Fixed-model bootstrap only. Not validation of a strategy.
